newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - Gold seen vulnerable below $343.00.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Gold seen vulnerable below $343.00.

text.p: SPOT NY CLOSE * SUPPORT * RESIST * RSI14 * MA10 * MA30
Gold needs to hold support at $343.00 an ounce to offset a fall towards $340.00, traders and chartists said on Monday.
Despite investment fund selling on Friday, silver was expected to consolidate around $4.70, while platinum was likely to find heavy ground on probes above $390.00, they added.
GOLD - Trading was expected to be with most of Europe closed for a publ;ic holiday. However, a breach of support at $343.00 an ounce might see a fall to $340.00, traders and chart analysts said.

Sentiment would remain dented by last week's news that Germany planned to revalue its reserves in a move linked to a budget deficit. Downside pressure was expected from chart signals that shrugged off upside momentum last week.
"With the technicals crossing down we are looking for further weakness," said Martin Squires of Rudolf Wolff, referring to the June Comex contract.
Squires was targeting a return to the 1997 low of $339.50.
"The German news did little for the market, which was starting to show signs of weakness...the fear of central bank sales is prominent," one London trader said.
In early trading on Monday gold was hovering above its 30-day moving average at $343.60, but the 10-day indicator at around $345.00 was likely to offer stiff resistance.
Further resistance was expected at $350.00, but that level was unlikely to be visited this week, traders said.
At 0713 GMT spot gold was quoted at $343.55/343.85, against Friday's London close of $344.50/$345.00.
SILVER - Despite a mauling from investment funds and longs on Friday, prices are likely to hover around $4.70.
But as turn weaker, traders and analysts expected downside pressure to emerge in the near term.
"With Europe closed I expect a quiet day for silver but during this week the market should turn lower," one trader said.
Traders suggested a fall to $4.60 if the market broke below support at $4.65.
Squires of Wolff said he expected a period of sustained weakness for silver with the technical indicators crossing down.
"Silver would needed to overcome resistance at $4.80/$4.85 to suggest a potential recovery, Squires said, referring to the September Comex contract.
The 10- and 30-day moving averages at $4.80 and $4.75 were seen as chart resistance.
At 0730 GMT spot silver was indicated at $4.69/$4.71, versus $4.70/$4.72.
PLATINUM - Seen struggling to overcome $390.00 but likely to tread water ahead of an influential Johnson Matthey report on platinum group metals later on Monday.
At 0730 GMT platinum was indicated at $388.50/$389.50, against $390.75/$391.75.
